title: Torsion vanishing for a compact group with full cyclic quotients
statement: Let G be a compact topological group, τ∈G such that the integer powers of τ are dense, and suppose for every positive N there is a continuous homomorphism χ_N:G→Multiplicative(ℤ/N) taking τ to 1. For every discrete G-module M whose underlying abelian group is torsion, and every integer q≥2, H^q(G,M)=Ext^q_DiscreteModule(G)(ℤ,M) is zero. No common annihilating integer for M is assumed.

source.place: proof, continuous-cochain/coinduced paragraph and finite-cyclic refinement and norm cancellation paragraphs

proof.text: If an open subgroup U contains τ, it contains every integer power of τ, so it is the whole group by density and closedness. More generally, let χ:G→ℤ/N be continuous with χ(τ)=1 and τ^N∈U. The set {χ≠0}∪U is closed and contains every integer power: a power outside its first part has exponent divisible by N, hence belongs to U. Density gives ker χ⊆U.

A smooth function f:G→A has open right stabilizer U. Compactness gives finite index and a positive a with τ^a∈U; it also gives finite image. Torsion gives e>0 killing all the finitely many values. Take N=ae and χ of order N. By the preceding step ker χ⊆U. If i(x) is the representative in [0,N) of χ(x), then x⁻¹τ^{i(x)}∈ker χ gives f(x)=F(i(x)), where F(j)=f(τ^j). The sequence F is a-periodic. Thus its sum on [0,N) is e times its sum on [0,a), which vanishes.

Set h(x)=Σ_{j<i(x)}F(j). This is fixed on the right by ker χ, so is smooth. Adding τ increases i(x) by one modulo N. The successive partial sums give h(xτ)-h(x)=f(x) away from wraparound; the vanishing full sum proves the same equation at wraparound. This also covers N=1 and the zero function.

For any discrete module X such that τ-1 is surjective, H¹(G,X)=0. To see this in the coinduced sequence 0→X→I(X)→Q(X)→0, represent an invariant quotient class by f. Then τf-f is the orbit function of an element x. Choose y with τy-y=x and subtract the orbit function of y. The resulting function is fixed by τ, hence by G using the first step; it still represents the class. Thus I(X)^G→Q(X)^G is surjective. The long exact Ext sequence gives H¹(G,X)=0 since I(X) is acyclic. The source proves coinduced acyclicity via the exact forget/coinduce adjunction: its Ext is Extⁿ_Ab(ℤ,A), zero for n>0 because ℤ is projective.

Let M be torsion. Every element of Q(M) has a representative f∈I(M); apply the finite cyclic primitive to f. This proves surjectivity of τ-1 on Q(M), and hence H¹(G,Q(M))=0 by the preceding step. Coinduced acyclicity and the long exact sequence give H²(G,M)=0. The quotient Q(M) is torsion: every smooth function has finite image and hence a positive annihilating integer. Induction using the same exact sequence gives H^q(G,M)=0 for every q≥2. All coinduced objects, exact sequences and Ext statements used here are already proved in WeilConjectures.RepresentationTheory.DiscreteModule.{Basic,CohomologicalDimension,Torsion}.

proof_origin.place: Finite cyclic partial sums at level ae replace the periodic-complex colimit implementation; coinduced dimension shifting is the proved source API. Adapted from the prime-power partial-sum argument in WeilConjectures.RepresentationTheory.DiscreteModule.Procyclic.
